evidence: Hit ABC defines from_dict, to_dict, is_valid_for_query — a minimal, honest contract. All 9 concrete hit types implement it cleanly.
MultiSearchQuery is a data-bag with 22+ optional fields covering the full Meilisearch query parameter set. Not an abstraction problem — mirrors the API spec directly.

converter_utils.py provides from_str, from_int, from_datetime etc. as named typed converters. These are not abstractions per se — they are named coercions. The naming is appropriate but the module lacks internal grouping.
QueryFieldsManager ABC has a single abstract method get_fields() returning list[str]. This is a thin, appropriate abstraction for the endpoint field registry pattern.
MultiSearchResult is Generic[HitType, FacetDistributionType, FacetStatsType] — appropriate use of generics for a typed container.

FacetDistribution and FacetStats ABCs exist but have minimal contract — concrete classes simply add typed fields. The abstraction cost is higher than the benefit (9 paired subclasses with no shared logic).
RetryConfig/TimeoutConfig are configuration dataclasses — not abstractions but value objects. Well-scoped.
CacheManager encapsulates requests_cache session lifecycle — an appropriate single-responsibility abstraction.
secure_logging.py provides get_secure_logger and mask_token — right-sized utilities.
from_dict pattern in models uses converter helpers but some models also do raw obj.get() for booleans and floats — a small inconsistency in the abstraction boundary.
abstraction_fitness.issues_preventing_higher_score: FacetDistribution/FacetStats ABCs with 9 paired subclasses and no shared logic add abstraction overhead without benefit; raw obj.get() mixed with converter helpers in model from_dict methods

abstraction_fitness.dimension_character: Abstractions are generally well-scoped and honest: Hit ABC, QueryFieldsManager, CacheManager, and the generic MultiSearchResult are all appropriate. The main weak point is the FacetDistribution/FacetStats ABC hierarchy which imposes 9 paired subclass pairs without shared logic, adding indirection cost with minimal benefit.
abstraction_fitness.score_rationale: Score of 75 reflects mostly fit abstractions with one structural cost (paired ABC hierarchies for facets) and a minor inconsistency (mixed raw obj.get() and converter helpers inside model from_dict). The generics usage is appropriate and the interface contracts are honest.

issues.summary: FacetDistribution and FacetStats ABCs generate 9 paired subclasses with no shared behavior, adding indirection without benefit
evidence: FacetDistribution ABC has no methods — it is only a marker type used for type-checking in generics
Each index has its own FacetDistribution subclass with only data fields and from_dict/to_dict
9 facet_distribution subclasses × 9 facet_stats subclasses = 18 files that are structurally identical except for field names
issues.suggestion: Replace the ABC hierarchy with a Generic TypeVar bound or Protocol. Consider a single FacetDistribution(dict[str, dict]) type with dynamic fields instead of 9 statically-typed subclasses, or use TypedDict for typed per-index facets without the ABC overhead.

issues.summary: Model from_dict methods mix raw obj.get() with converter helpers inconsistently
evidence: multi_search_query.py: show_ranking_score = obj.get('showRankingScore') — raw dict access instead of from_bool
Some hit models use obj.get() for boolean fields that should go through from_bool for consistent None-handling
issues.suggestion: Standardize all from_dict implementations to use converter helpers exclusively. Add from_bool to converter_utils if needed and update all raw obj.get() calls for boolean/float fields.

root_causes: type-system motivated ABC creation without behavior to abstract
incremental model growth mixing raw access with converters
